title: Testing cooler roofs
paragraphs: A school science team investigated whether roof colour affected classroom heat. Two unused storage huts were similar in size and stood beside each other. The students painted one roof white and left the other dark grey.

For ten school days, they recorded the temperature inside each hut at noon and at 3 p.m. They kept both doors shut during measurements and used the same two thermometers, swapping the instruments between huts each day.

The white-roofed hut was cooler in most, but not all, readings. On two cloudy afternoons, both huts had almost the same temperature. The students therefore described the white roof as promising rather than claiming that it would always keep a building cooler.

The principal asked why the thermometers had been swapped. The team explained that a small difference between the instruments could otherwise be mistaken for an effect of roof colour. Their method did not answer every question about real classrooms, but it made the limited comparison more trustworthy.
